trades.headline: Flip a dead IR body (A.J. Brown) and buried Stefon Diggs for a true starting QB in Jalen Hurts.
trades.summary: A.J. Brown is stuck on IR for ~6 weeks and Stefon Diggs is buried on a deep WR bench, so send both to Ben Hur Returns for Jalen Hurts, who becomes your starter with Jayden Daniels' return date unclear.

give: A.J. Brown (ankle) is on IR and expected out ~6 weeks per Ian Rapoport, producing nothing for you in the meantime.
Stefon Diggs (v1201) sits buried on your bench behind a WR group the league already rates as your deep position.
get: Jalen Hurts (v2084, PR5) is an every-week starting QB1, filling your thinnest roster spot the moment you need it.
Hurts' rushing floor is the buy-in case; analysts project positive regression after under 500 rush yards in a down 2025.
Jalen Coker (ankle, Questionable) was a limited-but-full practice participant Friday and is trending toward playing Week 3.
you: Hurts starts immediately at QB in place of Jayden Daniels, who dislocated his elbow again and has no firm return date.
Coker becomes a second-FLEX flier; you lose nothing in practice from A.J. Brown, who wasn't playing on IR anyway.
Converts a dead IR roster spot and a bench-only WR into a legitimate starting quarterback.
them: Ben Hur Returns (0-2) is thin at WR/TE and adds Brown plus Diggs, even if Brown's snaps don't start for weeks.
They already roster Tyler Shough as a starter-capable backup QB, so moving Hurts doesn't leave their lineup empty.

risks: Daniels dislocated the same elbow last year too and missed only 4 weeks then; a similarly quick return would make this look redundant.
Philadelphia lost O-line coach Jeff Stoutland and graded outside the top 16 on the line in 2025, a real threat to Hurts' rushing floor.
Coker's ankle has flared up multiple times already this season and could resurface in a later week.

trades.headline: Sell hurt Jayden Daniels and an inefficient DK Metcalf for Bryce Young's hot 648-yard, 6-TD start.
trades.summary: Daniels' elbow has no firm timeline and DK Metcalf can't turn target volume into yards, so both go to Strikes for Bryce Young, who's off to a top-14 caliber start, plus a depth running back.

give: Jayden Daniels dislocated the same elbow for a second time in 11 months; no surgery planned, but no firm return date either.
DK Metcalf led Pittsburgh in targets in Week 2 (9) but caught just 4 for 27 yards with a drop, shadowed by top corners.
get: Bryce Young has thrown for 648 yards, 6 TDs and just 1 INT through two games, in start-worthy Week 3 conversation.
Emanuel Wilson adds a depth flier at RB behind your already-deep Jonathan Taylor/Quinshon Judkins duo.
you: Young gives you a proven, in-form starter alongside newly acquired Jalen Hurts while Daniels' recovery stays open-ended.
Sheds Daniels' downside risk (repeat elbow dislocation, no set return) before further bad news erodes his value more.
them: Strikes are 0-2 and may be selling Young's hot two-game stretch for a bigger name in Metcalf plus a talent stash in Daniels.
They plug Metcalf straight into their flex spot as an upgrade over Deebo Samuel there, per their own lineup math.

risks: Bryce Young's 648-yard, 6-TD start over two games may not hold up once Carolina faces tougher pass defenses.
Emanuel Wilson's role in Seattle is unsettled; reports conflict on whether he or Jadarian Price leads the backfield.
Daniels missed only 4 weeks with this same elbow injury last year; a similarly quick return gives Strikes real value.
